model.name: Deployment
model.purpose: Context an agent needs to record, inspect and reason about a deployment: the identified act and standing fact of a release installed into a runtime environment target, with declared intent, execution state, history and evidence references.
model.scope_statement: A Deployment reifies the binding between a release (WM-SFT-008) and a runtime environment target (WM-SFT-010). It is not a plain edge: the same release may be deployed to the same target repeatedly, and each occurrence carries its own identity, desired state, state history and outcome. The model owns the deployment record, its identity, classification, binding keys, subject-specific deploy-time parameters, rollout intent, the deployment state machine, revision history, current-deployment resolution, rollback linkage, deployment time semantics, and references to authorization, gate and verification evidence produced elsewhere. It describes and records deployments; it does not orchestrate, execute, evaluate or enforce them, and it is not the system of record for release content, environment definition, policy decisions, telemetry or organizational audit trails.
in_scope: Deployment identity, classification and the release-to-target binding keys
Declared desired state, deploy-time parameter binding and rollout strategy intent
Deployment state machine, completion criteria, revision history, supersession and current-deployment resolution per target
Rollback and recovery linkage between deployment records
Deployment time semantics separating requested, started and completed times from observation and ingestion times
References to authorization, gate decisions and verification evidence produced by other systems
Delivery measurement over deployment records, plus record provenance, access, retention and interoperability projections
out_of_scope: Release identity, versioning, artifact content, SBOM and build provenance (owned by WM-SFT-008)
Runtime environment definition, topology, capacity, infrastructure inventory and environment lifecycle (owned by WM-SFT-010)
Execution of rollouts: orchestrators, reconciliation agents and traffic shifting mechanics
Policy evaluation, gate decision logic, enforcement engines and their runtime decisions
Runtime observability, alerting, incident and problem management, and service level objectives
Organizational audit-trail systems and evidentiary record keeping beyond this model's own records
CI/CD pipeline definition and pipeline run orchestration semantics
ITSM change record lifecycle, approval workflow engines and human identity management
Secret values, credentials and key material (only opaque references are carried)

boundary_notes.distinction: The release owns what is being installed: version, artifact digests, SBOM, build provenance and release approval. This model carries only a pinned release reference plus the digest used for binding integrity, and never reproduces release lifecycle or release-level functions.

The environment owns where software runs: environment identity, tier, topology, capacity and its own lifecycle. This model carries a pinned environment reference plus the deployment-specific target selector (cell, region, tenant slice) and never models environment creation, modification or deletion.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-SFT-002 parent software product or service model
boundary_notes.distinction: Product and service identity, ownership and commercial context are inherited from the parent. This model adds only the installed-into-environment occurrence.

Kubernetes Deployment objects, GitOps reconcilers and progressive-delivery controllers execute and observe rollouts. This model records declared intent and reported outcome as data; it grants no ownership of execution, reconciliation or traffic-shifting semantics.

SLSA verification summary attestations and equivalent gate verdicts are produced by external verifiers against external policies. This model records only the verdict reference, issuing verifier and verification time; it does not define evaluation, re-evaluate, or enforce.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Change management and configuration control process
boundary_notes.distinction: Change authorization, impact analysis and access restrictions for change are governed by the adopting Dimension's configuration change control regime. This model carries the authorization reference and its verdict, not the change workflow.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Software asset inventory and installed-software tagging
boundary_notes.distinction: Endpoint software identification tagging asserts what is installed on an asset. This model may reference such install evidence to corroborate a deployment, but tag production and asset inventory remain external.

sources.title: CDEvents Continuous Deployment Events
sources.version_or_date: spec main branch; continuous deployment subjects at 0.3.0; CDEvents release line v0.5.0
sources.relevance: Defines the environment and service subjects and the deployed, upgraded, rolledback, removed and published predicates, with required id, environment and purl artifactId fields; anchors deployment classification, binding and event vocabulary.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry Semantic Conventions - Deployment attribute registry
sources.relevance: Provides the stable deployment.environment.name attribute and the still-unstable deployment.id, deployment.name and deployment.status attributes, plus the note that environment name does not affect service uniqueness constraints.

sources.title: Kubernetes Documentation - Deployments
sources.relevance: Normative first-party model of desired state versus observed status, RollingUpdate and Recreate strategies, revisionHistoryLimit, progressDeadlineSeconds, minReadySeconds, pause/resume and the Progressing, Complete and Failed status conditions.

sources.title: OpenGitOps Principles v1.0.0
sources.relevance: States that desired state must be declarative, versioned and immutable with complete version history, pulled automatically and continuously reconciled; grounds the declared-intent and history findings and the boundary against reconciliation execution.

sources.title: SLSA Verification Summary Attestation (VSA)
sources.version_or_date: SLSA v1.0 (page notes v1.2 is the latest release line)
sources.relevance: Defines a verifier-produced verdict with subject digest, verifier URI, timeVerified, resourceUri, policy, verificationResult and verifiedLevels; supports carrying gate verdicts by reference without owning evaluation.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Requires archiving and protecting each software release, configuring software with secure settings by default, and verifying software integrity before use; grounds pre-deployment integrity evidence and secure default parameter binding.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.version_or_date: Revision 5, September 2020 with updates through 10 December 2020; control release 5.2.0, 27 August 2025
sources.relevance: Configuration Management family provides baseline configuration, configuration change control and access restrictions for change; Audit and Accountability and System and Information Integrity families ground access logging and software integrity verification.

sources.title: NISTIR 8060, Guidelines for the Creation of Interoperable Software Identification (SWID) Tags
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Implements ISO/IEC 19770-2 software identification tags as endpoint-level evidence that a software product is installed; supports corroborating a deployment against observed installed-software facts.

sources.title: Deployment and Configuration of Component-based Distributed Applications (DEPL), Version 4.0
sources.relevance: Standardizes metadata and interfaces for deploying and configuring component-based applications into heterogeneous distributed target systems; the oldest normative anchor for a deployment plan bound to a target domain.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026, Systems and software engineering - Software life cycle processes
sources.version_or_date: 2026 edition; technically revised, cancels and replaces ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2017
sources.relevance: Defines the software life cycle process framework covering supply, operation, maintenance and disposal, including transition of software into an operational environment; frames deployment as a life cycle process rather than a tool artifact.

sources.title: SPDX Specification 3.0.1 - Core LifecycleScopeType vocabulary
sources.relevance: Provides build, design, development, runtime, test and other lifecycle scopes for relationships; shows that runtime scoping exists for relationships but no deployment entity is defined, marking an interoperability boundary.

sources.title: DORA software delivery metrics: the four keys
sources.relevance: Defines change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time, change fail rate and deployment rework rate; these are computed over deployment records and constrain the required timestamp and outcome fields.

sources.title: Argo Rollouts - Canary Deployment Strategy
sources.relevance: Documents progressive delivery mechanics: setWeight and pause steps, analysis, manual promotion and abort with scale-down delay; grounds the rollout strategy vocabulary while remaining an execution concern outside this model.

bundles.name: Deployment identity and subject binding
bundles.description: What counts as one deployment, how it is identified and classified, and how it binds a referenced release to a referenced environment target and to the resulting running instances.
bundles.rationale: CDEvents models a deployed service as a subject that must carry an id, an environment reference and a purl artifactId, and OpenTelemetry keeps environment name separate from service instance identity; a deployment therefore needs its own identity distinct from both referenced subjects.

layers.name: Deployment definition, identity and classification
layers.description: The definitional core: the unit of deployment, its identifier rules and the kind of deployment being recorded.

findings.name: Unit of deployment and record granularity
findings.description: Defines what is counted as one deployment (one release, one target scope, one intent) and distinguishes a deployment occurrence from the deployable object, the pipeline run and the running service instance.

questions.text: What exactly constitutes one deployment record, and what is the smallest change that starts a new one rather than updating an existing one?
answer_data: Trigger conditions that mint a new deployment
Conditions that update an existing deployment in place

questions.text: When a single release is rolled out to many targets or many components at once, is that one deployment or many, and how is the grouping represented?
answer_data: Fan-out policy (single record versus one per target)

questions.text: How is a deployment record distinguished from the pipeline run that produced it and from the service instance that results from it?
Does a configuration-only or parameter-only change with no release change produce a deployment record?

data_elements.name: deployment_unit_scope
data_elements.description: Declared granularity of the record: single target, target group or fleet campaign.

data_elements.name: deployment_group_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a parent deployment group or campaign when a release is fanned out across many targets.

data_elements.name: originating_pipeline_run_reference
data_elements.description: Opaque reference to the pipeline run or automation execution that requested the deployment; the run's own semantics stay external.

artifacts.name: Deployment record
artifacts.description: The canonical record of one deployment occurrence, holding identity, binding references, declared intent, terminal state and evidence references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the authoritative master-system deployment identifier from the system of record, carried with its issuing system reference; falls back to a governed IRI, then to a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID.

findings.name: Deployment identifier and correlation keys
findings.description: How a deployment is identified across systems, including the priority of authoritative identifiers over minted ones and the natural keys used to reconcile duplicate reports of the same deployment.

questions.text: Which system is the authoritative master system for this deployment identifier, and what identifier does it assign?
When no authoritative identifier exists, what governed identifier or minted surrogate is used and who minted it?
What natural key set is used to detect that two reports describe the same deployment occurrence?
answer_data: Natural key tuple (release digest, target selector, requested time window)

questions.text: Is the deployment identifier stable across retries, resumed rollouts and orchestrator restarts?

data_elements.name: deployment_identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the deployment, recorded together with the issuing system so that priority can be evaluated.

data_elements.name: identifier_issuing_system
data_elements.description: Reference to the system that assigned the deployment identifier and the identifier tier used.

data_elements.name: attempt_sequence_number
data_elements.description: Monotonic attempt counter distinguishing retries of the same declared intent.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is a rule set plus a small set of key fields carried on the deployment record defined in the sibling finding; minting a separate identity artifact would duplicate that record and create a second, competing identifier surface.

findings.name: Deployment kind and intent classification
findings.description: The controlled vocabulary distinguishing initial install, upgrade, rollback, configuration-only change, redeploy and removal, aligned to the CDEvents service predicates.

questions.text: Which deployment kind applies, and which controlled vocabulary term is used for it?
Is this a planned deployment, an emergency or hotfix deployment, or unplanned rework triggered by an incident?
Is the deployment declared reversible, and what is the declared reversal path?
answer_data: Irreversible-step reasons such as data migration

data_elements.name: deployment_kind
data_elements.description: Controlled term for the deployment kind: initial-install, upgrade, rollback, configuration-change, redeploy or removal.

data_elements.name: unplanned_rework_flag
data_elements.description: Whether the deployment is unplanned work resulting from a production incident, as required to compute deployment rework rate.

data_elements.name: declared_reversibility
data_elements.description: Whether the deployment is declared reversible and by which declared method.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a small set of coded values on the deployment record plus a mapping table into external vocabularies; the mapping table is already carried by the interoperability alignment finding, so no separate artifact is warranted here.

layers.name: Referenced subject bindings
layers.description: The pinned references to the release and to the environment target, and the correlation to the instances that result from the deployment.

findings.name: Release reference and binding integrity
findings.description: How the deployed release is referenced and pinned, carrying the reference, the artifact coordinate and the digest used to prove the binding, without reproducing release lifecycle.

questions.text: Which release is bound to this deployment, and by what pinned reference and artifact coordinate?
answer_data: Package URL or equivalent artifact coordinate

questions.text: Which content digest and algorithm were recorded at binding time to prove that the intended release was the one deployed?
What happens to this deployment record if the referenced release is later revised, withdrawn or re-tagged upstream?
answer_data: Immutability rule for the pinned reference
Flag for superseded or withdrawn release

questions.text: Can one deployment bind more than one release or component, and how is the set bounded?

data_elements.name: release_reference
data_elements.description: Pinned reference to the release record in WM-SFT-008; release attributes are not copied.

data_elements.name: artifact_coordinate
data_elements.description: Package URL or equivalent coordinate identifying the deployed artifact, as required by the CDEvents service subject.

data_elements.name: binding_content_digest
data_elements.description: Algorithm-qualified digest of the artifact recorded at binding time for integrity checking.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The relation to WM-SFT-008 is REFERENCE, so this finding may carry only the reference, binding keys and digests. Producing a local artifact describing the release would restate target-owned content and risk drifting from the release system of record.

findings.name: Environment reference and target placement
findings.description: The pinned environment reference plus the deployment-specific target selector describing which cells, regions, tenants or device groups received the release.

questions.text: Which runtime environment is targeted, and by what pinned reference and environment tier name?
Within that environment, which subset of targets was selected for this deployment?
answer_data: Enumerated target node or cluster references

questions.text: In which geographic or jurisdictional locations did the deployed instances actually run as a result of this deployment?
Which tenants, customers or device cohorts were in scope, and were any explicitly excluded?
answer_data: Scope percentage where cohorts are sampled

data_elements.name: environment_reference
data_elements.description: Pinned reference to the runtime environment record in WM-SFT-010.

data_elements.name: target_selector
data_elements.description: Deployment-specific selector or enumeration naming the subset of the environment that received the release.

data_elements.name: resulting_placement_regions
data_elements.description: Region, zone or jurisdiction codes where the deployed instances ran, as reported at completion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Environment structure is owned by WM-SFT-010 under a REFERENCE relation; only the reference and the deployment-specific selector and reported placement facts belong here, and those are field-level data rather than a standalone artifact.

findings.name: Deployed instance and installed-software correlation
findings.description: How the deployment record correlates to the concrete running or installed instances it produced, so that observed installed software can be reconciled to a deployment.

questions.text: Which service instance identifiers, container identities or device identifiers are attributable to this deployment?
What installed-software evidence on the target corroborates that this release is present?
answer_data: Evidence collection time and collector reference

questions.text: How is an observed running instance attributed to exactly one deployment when several deployments overlap in time?

data_elements.name: deployed_instance_references
data_elements.description: Identifiers of the instances attributed to this deployment, using the runtime system's own instance identity scheme.

data_elements.name: installed_software_evidence_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to endpoint software identification tag evidence corroborating the installation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are correlation keys and evidence pointers only. The tags and telemetry themselves are produced and owned by asset inventory and observability systems, so materialising them locally would duplicate externally owned records.

bundles.name: Declared intent and deployment configuration
bundles.description: The declarative desired state for the deployment, the deploy-time parameters bound to it, and the planned rollout strategy and window.
bundles.rationale: GitOps principles require desired state to be declarative, versioned and immutable, OMG DEPL standardises a deployment plan bound to a target domain, and SSDF requires software to be configured with secure settings by default.

layers.name: Declared desired state and parameters
layers.description: What was declared to be true after the deployment, and which subject-specific parameter values were bound at deploy time.

findings.name: Desired state declaration and its version
findings.description: The declarative statement of the intended post-deployment state, its immutable version reference and its source of truth, kept distinct from the reconciliation that applies it.

questions.text: Where is the declarative desired state held, and which immutable version of it does this deployment assert?
What does the declaration assert about the target after deployment, in format-neutral terms?
answer_data: Declared component set and replica or instance counts

questions.text: How is divergence between the declared desired state and the reported actual state recorded on the deployment?
answer_data: Drift observation reference and observation time

questions.text: Who is authorised to change the desired state declaration for this target, and is the change recorded as a new deployment?

data_elements.name: desired_state_declaration_reference
data_elements.description: Immutable, versioned reference to the declarative desired state asserted by this deployment.

data_elements.name: desired_state_digest
data_elements.description: Algorithm-qualified digest of the canonical desired state declaration at the moment it was bound.

data_elements.name: drift_status
data_elements.description: Recorded status of divergence between declared desired state and the last reported actual state.

artifacts.name: Deployment desired-state declaration
artifacts.description: The versioned, immutable declaration of intended post-deployment state bound to this deployment, held as a content-addressed reference set rather than a live configuration store.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the source-of-truth revision identifier from the authoritative declaration store plus a content digest; where no such store exists, by a governed IRI minted by the adopting Dimension.

findings.name: Deploy-time parameter and secret-reference binding
findings.description: The subject-specific configuration values, feature toggles and opaque secret references bound at deployment time, together with the secure-default baseline they deviate from.

questions.text: Which parameter keys and values were bound for this deployment, and which deviate from the documented secure default configuration?
How are credentials and key material referenced without being carried in the deployment record?
Which bound parameters are sensitive or personal-data-relevant and therefore require redaction on read?
Which parameter values were actually effective at completion, as opposed to merely requested?

data_elements.name: parameter_binding_set
data_elements.description: Set of deploy-time parameter keys with values or opaque references, each carrying a sensitivity classification.

data_elements.name: secret_reference_set
data_elements.description: Opaque references to secrets required by the deployment; values are never stored in this model.

data_elements.name: baseline_configuration_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the secure default or baseline configuration against which deviations are recorded.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Parameter bindings are field-level data on the deployment record and frequently contain sensitive values, so they are held inline with per-field sensitivity classification and redaction rather than materialised as a separate distributable artifact.

layers.name: Rollout strategy and deployment plan
layers.description: The declared rollout method and the planned timing, sequencing and constraints for carrying it out.

findings.name: Declared rollout strategy
findings.description: The strategy declared for this deployment, such as recreate, rolling update, blue-green or canary with staged weights and pauses, recorded as intent rather than as executable mechanics.

questions.text: Which rollout strategy was declared, and which strategy-specific limits such as surge, unavailability or step weights were set?
answer_data: Ordered step definitions with weights and pause durations

questions.text: Which pauses in the declared strategy require an explicit promotion decision rather than elapsing automatically?
Under what declared conditions is the rollout to be aborted, and what does abort mean for the recorded state?
Does the declared strategy accept service interruption, and was that interruption expected and communicated?

data_elements.name: rollout_strategy_type
data_elements.description: Declared strategy code: recreate, rolling-update, blue-green, canary or other.

data_elements.name: rollout_step_definitions
data_elements.description: Ordered declared steps with traffic weight, pause duration and promotion requirement.

data_elements.name: availability_limits
data_elements.description: Declared maximum surge, maximum unavailable and minimum ready duration values.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The strategy is declared intent captured as coded fields and an ordered step list on the deployment record; the executable controller configuration that realises it is owned by the orchestrator and must not be mirrored here.

findings.name: Deployment plan, sequencing and permitted window
findings.description: The planned schedule, ordering dependencies among deployments, and the freeze or maintenance windows constraining when the deployment may proceed.

questions.text: Within which permitted window was this deployment scheduled, and in which local offset is that window expressed?
answer_data: Planned window start and end with explicit offset
Window type such as maintenance or freeze exemption

questions.text: Which other deployments must complete before or after this one, and what happens if a predecessor fails?
What plan-level mapping of components to target nodes was declared before execution began?
answer_data: Assignment method such as manual or solver-generated

questions.text: Did execution deviate from the plan, and what deviation was recorded?

data_elements.name: planned_window
data_elements.description: Planned start and end instants for the deployment, each with explicit offset.

data_elements.name: plan_dependency_references
data_elements.description: References to predecessor or successor deployments with the ordering constraint type.

data_elements.name: component_target_assignment
data_elements.description: Declared mapping of deployable components to target nodes within the target domain.

artifacts.name: Deployment plan
artifacts.description: The pre-execution plan binding components to targets with sequencing, permitted window and declared constraints, in the sense of a standardised deployment plan for a target domain.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the planning system's own plan identifier where one exists, carried with the issuing system reference; otherwise by a governed IRI, with the covering deployment identifier as a mandatory back-reference.

bundles.name: Execution state, history and time
bundles.description: The recorded state of the deployment over its life, the revision history that determines which deployment is current for a target, rollback linkage, and the time semantics that make all of it comparable.
bundles.rationale: Kubernetes distinguishes desired spec from observed status with Progressing, Complete and Failed conditions and a bounded revision history; GitOps requires complete version history; DORA metrics depend on precise deployment timestamps and outcomes.

layers.name: Deployment state model
layers.description: The state vocabulary, permitted transitions and the criteria by which a deployment is judged complete or failed.

findings.name: Deployment state vocabulary and transitions
findings.description: The controlled set of deployment states, which are terminal, and which transitions are permitted, recorded as an append-only transition history.

questions.text: Which states can a deployment occupy, and which of them are terminal?
Which state transitions are permitted, and which actor or source may assert each of them?
answer_data: Asserting actor or system per transition

questions.text: How is a paused or awaiting-promotion deployment represented, and does pause time count toward deployment duration?
When the state is reported by an external orchestrator, how is the reported value mapped into this model's vocabulary?
answer_data: Mapping rule to local state code

data_elements.name: current_state
data_elements.description: Current deployment state code from the controlled vocabulary.

data_elements.name: state_transition_entry
data_elements.description: Append-only transition entry with prior state, new state, asserting source, reason and transition instant.

data_elements.name: source_reported_status
data_elements.description: Status string exactly as reported by the external orchestrator, retained unmapped for traceability.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The state model is a vocabulary and transition rule set expressed as coded fields plus append-only entries; the durable serial record of those entries is carried by the deployment history ledger artifact, so declaring a second artifact here would duplicate it.

findings.name: Progress reporting and completion criteria
findings.description: The declared criteria by which a deployment is judged to have progressed, completed or failed, and how externally observed progress reports are recorded against them.

questions.text: What criteria must be satisfied for this deployment to be declared complete, and who declared them?
What deadline applies before a non-progressing deployment is treated as failed, and what happened when it elapsed?
Which observed counts or signals were reported against the declared criteria, and by which reporting system?
answer_data: Observed ready, updated and available counts

questions.text: When a deployment failed, what reason code was recorded and was that reason produced locally or received from the orchestrator?

data_elements.name: completion_criteria
data_elements.description: Declared criteria and thresholds that define successful completion of the deployment.

data_elements.name: progress_deadline_duration
data_elements.description: Maximum permitted duration without progress before the deployment is treated as failed.

data_elements.name: progress_observation_entry
data_elements.description: Recorded observation of progress counts or signals with the reporting system and observation instant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Progress signals are produced by the orchestrator and observability stack under a REFERENCE boundary; this model records only the declared criteria and the received observation entries as inline data, and must not become a store of runtime telemetry.

layers.name: History, supersession and rollback linkage
layers.description: How deployment records accumulate into a history per target, which one is current, and how rollbacks and recoveries are linked.

findings.name: Revision history and current-deployment resolution
findings.description: The ordered history of deployments for a target, the rule that resolves which deployment is currently in effect, and the bounded retention of superseded revisions.

questions.text: Which deployment is currently in effect for a given environment target, and by what deterministic rule is that resolved?
How are deployments to the same target ordered when their reported timestamps are equal, missing or out of order?
How many superseded revisions are retained in usable form, and what is retained once a revision falls outside that bound?
answer_data: Reduced record content after the bound

questions.text: How is a gap in the history detected when deployments occurred without being recorded?

data_elements.name: revision_sequence_number
data_elements.description: Monotonic sequence number of this deployment within the history of its target.

data_elements.name: superseded_by_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the deployment that superseded this one for the same target.

data_elements.name: is_current_for_target
data_elements.description: Derived flag indicating that this deployment is the one currently in effect for its target, valid as of a stated instant.

artifacts.name: Deployment history ledger
artifacts.description: Append-only ordered ledger of deployment occurrences and state transitions for one environment target, supporting current-deployment resolution and complete version history.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the target reference plus a zero-padded monotonic sequence per target; the sequence rather than a timestamp establishes order, and each entry back-references its deployment identifier.

findings.name: Rollback, roll-forward and recovery linkage
findings.description: The typed links between a remediating deployment and the deployment it reverts or repairs, together with the recovery outcome as reported.

questions.text: Which prior deployment does this rollback revert, and which release state is restored as a result?
What triggered the remediation, and was it an automated abort or a human decision?
How long did recovery take from the failed deployment to a restored serving state, and against which two recorded instants is that measured?
Was the rollback complete, partial or unsuccessful, and what residual state was left behind?

data_elements.name: rollback_of_reference
data_elements.description: Typed reference from a remediating deployment to the deployment it reverts.

data_elements.name: recovery_interval
data_elements.description: Recorded failure onset and recovery completion instants used to derive failed deployment recovery time.

data_elements.name: rollback_outcome
data_elements.description: Coded outcome of the remediation: complete, partial or unsuccessful.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Rollback linkage is a set of typed edges and instants between existing deployment records; representing it as its own artifact would create a parallel structure competing with the deployment history ledger.

layers.name: Deployment time semantics
layers.description: The distinct instants that a deployment record carries and the rules that keep them comparable across systems and jurisdictions.

findings.name: Event time versus observation and ingestion time
findings.description: Separates when the deployment was requested, started, completed or superseded from when those facts were observed and ingested, and fixes the representation rules for all of them.

questions.text: Which distinct instants are recorded for this deployment, and which of them are mandatory?
answer_data: Requested, started, completed and superseded instants
Null handling rule for unknown instants

questions.text: When was each reported fact observed by the reporting system and ingested into this model, and how is that kept separate from the event instant?
answer_data: Separation rule and prohibition on back-filling

questions.text: In which offset was each instant originally expressed, and is that original offset preserved alongside any derived normalised value?
Which upstream instant anchors change lead time for this deployment, and is that anchor owned by this model or referenced?

data_elements.name: deployment_event_instants
data_elements.description: Requested, started, completed and superseded instants, each with explicit seconds and offset.

data_elements.name: observation_instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the reporting system observed the fact, distinct from the event instant.

data_elements.name: ingestion_instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the fact was ingested into this model's records.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Time semantics are representation rules and timestamp fields attached to records defined elsewhere in this model; they have no independent artifact and are enforced through the service-layer timestamp rule instead.

bundles.name: Authorisation and assurance evidence
bundles.description: Who authorised the deployment, which gate verdicts were relied upon, and which integrity and post-deployment verification evidence is referenced.
bundles.rationale: Configuration change control and access restrictions for change require recorded authorisation; SSDF requires release integrity verification before use; SLSA verification summary attestations supply verifier-issued verdicts that may be referenced but not re-owned.

layers.name: Authorisation to deploy
layers.description: The recorded authority for the deployment and the references to gate decisions relied upon at the deployment boundary.

findings.name: Deployment authorisation and accountable actors
findings.description: The recorded authorisation for this deployment, the change or approval reference relied upon, the actors involved, and the separation-of-duties assertion, all carried as references to externally governed decisions.

questions.text: Which change or approval record authorised this deployment, and what was its recorded verdict at the time of binding?
Which human or automated actors requested, approved and initiated the deployment, and in which roles?
Was separation of duties satisfied between the actor who approved and the actor who initiated, and how is a violation recorded?
If normal authorisation was bypassed under an emergency procedure, what retrospective authorisation is required and by when?
answer_data: Emergency bypass flag and procedure reference

data_elements.name: authorization_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally owned change or approval record that authorised the deployment, with its verdict as received.

data_elements.name: actor_role_assignments
data_elements.description: Actor references with their role in this deployment: requester, approver or initiator.

data_elements.name: emergency_bypass_flag
data_elements.description: Whether normal authorisation was bypassed under an emergency procedure.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Authorisation records, approval workflows and actor identities are owned by the adopting Dimension's change control and identity systems; this model carries only references, roles and received verdicts, so materialising a local authorisation artifact would clone an externally owned record.

findings.name: Deployment gate decision references
findings.description: References to verdicts issued by external verifiers or policy engines that were relied upon at the deployment boundary, recorded without any local evaluation, re-evaluation or enforcement.

questions.text: Which gate verdicts were relied upon for this deployment, and which verifier issued each one?
Against which policy identifier and version was each relied-upon verdict issued, and where does that policy live?
answer_data: Statement that policy content is not held locally

questions.text: How recent must a gate verdict be to remain valid for this deployment, and what happens when it is stale?
Was any failing or missing gate verdict overridden, and what override record justifies proceeding?

data_elements.name: gate_verdict_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an externally issued verdict, carrying issuer, subject digest, policy identifier and verification instant.

data_elements.name: gate_verdict_value
data_elements.description: Verdict value exactly as received from the issuing verifier, never recomputed locally.

data_elements.name: gate_override_record_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally owned override justification when a gate was bypassed.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Gate verdicts are attestations produced and owned by external verifiers. Reproducing them locally would imply ownership of evaluation and enforcement semantics that this model explicitly disclaims, so only references, issuers and received values are held.

layers.name: Integrity and verification evidence
layers.description: Evidence referenced before deployment to prove the intended release was deployed, and the outcome recorded after deployment.

findings.name: Pre-deployment integrity evidence
findings.description: The evidence relied upon before installation that the artifact bound to the deployment is authentic and unmodified, referenced from the archived release and signature or attestation sources.

questions.text: What integrity check was performed before installation, and was its result recorded as passed, failed or not performed?
answer_data: Check instant and performing system reference

questions.text: Which signature, attestation or archived-release reference supports the authenticity of the deployed artifact?
What is recorded when the digest presented at install time differs from the digest bound at planning time?
answer_data: Mismatch flag and both digest values

data_elements.name: integrity_check_result
data_elements.description: Coded result of the pre-deployment integrity check, with the checking system reference.

data_elements.name: integrity_attestation_references
data_elements.description: References to signatures, attestations or archived release locations supporting authenticity.

artifacts.name: Deployment verification evidence index
artifacts.description: An index of pointers assembled by this model that lists every integrity and gate evidence item relied upon for one deployment, with issuer, subject digest and verification instant; it contains references and never copies of the evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the covering deployment identifier from the authoritative master system; the index carries no identity independent of the deployment it serves.

findings.name: Post-deployment verification outcome and acceptance
findings.description: The recorded outcome of post-deployment checks and the acceptance decision closing the deployment, captured as received verdicts rather than as executed tests or live health monitoring.

questions.text: What post-deployment verification verdict was received, from which checking system, and at what instant?
Who accepted the deployment as successful, and on what basis was that acceptance recorded?
Which defects, degradations or incidents were attributed to this deployment after completion, and how are they referenced?
Is there a declared observation period after completion before the deployment is considered stable, and when does it end?

data_elements.name: post_deployment_verdict
data_elements.description: Verdict received from post-deployment checks, with the checking system reference and instant.

data_elements.name: attributed_incident_references
data_elements.description: References to externally owned incident or defect records attributed to this deployment.

data_elements.name: change_failure_flag
data_elements.description: Whether the deployment required immediate intervention such as rollback or hotfix, as needed for change fail rate.

artifacts.name: Deployment completion report
artifacts.description: The closing summary of one deployment: terminal state, effective placement, received verification verdicts, acceptance decision and attributed follow-up references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the covering deployment identifier from the authoritative master system, with a content digest over its canonical form; it is issued once per terminal deployment and superseded rather than edited.

bundles.name: Delivery measurement and record governance
bundles.description: Metrics derived from deployment records, and the provenance, access, sensitivity and retention rules governing those records.
bundles.rationale: DORA delivery metrics are computed over deployment records and constrain which fields must exist; audit, access restriction and record-keeping controls govern how those records are read and retained.

layers.name: Delivery performance measurement
layers.description: Metrics computed over this model's own deployment records, with their windows, denominators and validity conditions.

findings.name: Delivery metrics and measurement validity
findings.description: The metric definitions computed from deployment records, the population and window they apply to, and the record-completeness conditions under which the results are valid.

questions.text: Which delivery metrics are computed from these records, and by which exact definition and denominator?
Over which time window and target population is each metric computed, and in which offset is the window expressed?
answer_data: Window start and end with explicit offset

questions.text: Which record-completeness conditions must hold before a computed metric may be published, and what is reported when they fail?
Which deployments are excluded from metric populations, and on what documented basis?

data_elements.name: metric_definition_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the exact metric definition and version used, so that recomputation is reproducible.

data_elements.name: metric_value
data_elements.description: Computed metric value with its unit, window and population size.

data_elements.name: record_coverage_ratio
data_elements.description: Share of in-scope deployments with all fields required by the metric present, used to qualify the result.

artifacts.name: Delivery metrics report
artifacts.description: A periodic report of delivery metrics computed over this model's deployment records, carrying window bounds, population filters, coverage ratio and documented exclusions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the reporting scope reference plus a zero-padded monotonic sequence per scope; the covering window is carried as explicit start and end fields rather than encoded into the name.

layers.name: Record provenance, access and retention
layers.description: How deployment records came to exist, who may read them and at what sensitivity, and how they are disposed of.

findings.name: Deployment record provenance and reconciliation
findings.description: The origin, capture path and trust level of each deployment record, including whether it was asserted by a pipeline, reconciled from observed state, or entered manually.

questions.text: Which system asserted this deployment record, and through which capture path did it reach the model?
answer_data: Capture path code such as event feed, reconciliation or manual entry

questions.text: What confidence level is attached to the record, and which fields are inferred rather than asserted?
answer_data: Inferred field list with inference basis

questions.text: When observed installed state contradicts the recorded deployment, which source wins and what correction entry is written?
Which parts of a terminal deployment record are immutable, and how are later corrections expressed?

data_elements.name: asserting_system_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the system that asserted the record, with the capture path used.

data_elements.name: record_confidence_level
data_elements.description: Confidence classification for the record, distinguishing asserted from inferred content.

data_elements.name: correction_entry_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a superseding entry that corrects a previously recorded fact without mutating it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance is metadata carried on records defined elsewhere in this model. It is deliberately not made an artifact, because a separate provenance document would invite confusion with the adopting Dimension's audit-trail system, whose semantics this model does not own.

findings.name: Record access, sensitivity and redaction
findings.description: The sensitivity classification of deployment record content and the rules governing who may read which parts, including production target detail and parameter bindings.

questions.text: What sensitivity classification applies to each part of the deployment record, and who set it?
Which roles may read production target placement, parameter bindings and evidence references, and at what scope?
answer_data: Scope level (bundle, layer, finding or artifact)

questions.text: Under what emergency conditions may normal read restrictions be bypassed, and what must be recorded when they are?
answer_data: Post-hoc review requirement and due instant

data_elements.name: sensitivity_classification
data_elements.description: Sensitivity class assigned to a field group of the deployment record.

data_elements.name: access_grant_entry
data_elements.description: Role, scope and validity of a read grant over part of this model's records.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Access control decisions are expressed as classification labels and grant entries evaluated by the adopting Dimension's access system. This model records the classification and the grant declarations only, and does not own enforcement, so no distributable artifact is appropriate.

findings.name: Retention, disposition and tombstones
findings.description: How long deployment records are kept, what reduced form survives disposition, and which external policy owns the execution of deletion.

questions.text: What retention period applies to a deployment record, and from which instant is it measured?
What minimal tombstone survives disposition, and which fields are purged?
What suspends disposition, such as legal hold or an open investigation, and who may set and release it?
When a referenced release or environment record is deleted upstream, what happens to this deployment record?
answer_data: Owner of the upstream deletion decision

data_elements.name: retention_period
data_elements.description: Duration for which the full deployment record is retained, with the policy reference that sets it.

data_elements.name: disposition_tombstone
data_elements.description: Reduced surviving record marking that a deployment existed and was disposed of, with the disposition instant.

data_elements.name: legal_hold_flag
data_elements.description: Whether disposition is suspended by a hold, with the reason and the setting authority.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention is a rule set plus a small tombstone structure attached to existing records. Physical destruction is executed by the adopting Dimension's records-management and storage policy, so producing a local disposition artifact would misattribute ownership of the deletion act.

bundles.name: Interoperability and external alignment
bundles.description: How deployment records are projected onto, and reconciled with, external deployment vocabularies without asserting conformance.
bundles.rationale: CDEvents, OpenTelemetry, SPDX and software identification tagging each describe part of the deployment surface with incompatible identifier schemes and stability levels, so alignments must be recorded explicitly with mapping evidence.

layers.name: Standards alignment and identifier exchange
layers.description: The recorded mappings to external standards, the identifier schemes exchanged, and the known points where mappings are lossy.

findings.name: External standard alignments and identifier exchange
findings.description: The declared alignments to external deployment vocabularies, the identifier and digest schemes used to exchange deployment facts, and the explicit statement that alignment is not conformance.

questions.text: Which external vocabulary terms does each local element map to, and at which version of that vocabulary?
answer_data: Local element to external term mapping

questions.text: Where is a mapping lossy, approximate or unavailable, and what is recorded in place of a value?
answer_data: Lossy mapping list with loss description

questions.text: Which identifier and digest schemes are exchanged with external systems, and how are they normalised on ingest?
answer_data: Identifier scheme list such as package coordinates, instance identifiers and content digests

questions.text: Is conformance to any external specification asserted, and if so on what cited evidence?
answer_data: Stability level of the external terms relied upon

data_elements.name: alignment_mapping_entry
data_elements.description: One mapping from a local element to an external vocabulary term, with the external version and loss notes.

data_elements.name: external_term_stability
data_elements.description: Stability level of each external term relied upon, so that unstable terms are not treated as normative.

data_elements.name: exchanged_identifier_scheme
data_elements.description: Named identifier or digest scheme exchanged with an external system, with its normalisation rule.

artifacts.name: Deployment interoperability mapping set
artifacts.description: The maintained set of alignments between this model's elements and external deployment vocabularies, recording external versions, stability levels, mapping direction and known losses.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a governed IRI minted under the adopting Dimension's namespace for this model, versioned independently of the deployment records it maps.

functions.name: Register deployment record
functions.description: Create a deployment record binding a pinned release reference to an environment target with a declared intent, without initiating any execution.
inputs: Deployment kind and desired state declaration reference
preconditions: Release and environment references resolve
Identifier priority rules can be satisfied
Deployment kind is in the controlled vocabulary
effects: A new deployment record exists in a non-terminal state
The record is appended to the target's history ledger

functions.name: Record deployment state transition
functions.description: Append a state transition asserted by an external orchestrator or actor, mapping the reported status into the local vocabulary and retaining the raw value.
inputs: Reported status value and asserting source
preconditions: Deployment record exists
Transition is permitted from the current state
Event and observation instants carry explicit offsets

functions.name: Resolve current deployment for a target
functions.description: Determine deterministically which deployment record is currently in effect for a given environment target as of a stated instant.
preconditions: A history ledger exists for the target
Revision ordering rules are defined
effects: Ambiguities are flagged for stewardship review

functions.name: Ingest observed state report
functions.description: Ingest an externally produced report of observed installed or running state and record its agreement or divergence with the declared desired state.
inputs: Observed state report and reporting system reference
outputs: Gap marker when no deployment record explains the observation
preconditions: Reporting system is a recognised source
Report carries an observation instant with explicit offset
effects: Drift status is updated on the affected deployment
Unexplained observations create a history gap marker

functions.name: Link rollback or recovery deployment
functions.description: Establish the typed link between a remediating deployment and the deployment it reverts or repairs, and record the recovery interval.
inputs: Failure onset and recovery completion instants
preconditions: Both deployment records exist and share a target
The reverted deployment has a recorded failure or defect attribution
effects: Rollback linkage is available for metric computation
Change failure classification is set on the reverted deployment

functions.name: Attach verification evidence reference
functions.description: Attach a reference to an externally issued integrity, gate or post-deployment verdict, recording issuer, policy identifier and verification instant without evaluating or recomputing it.
inputs: Evidence reference with issuer and subject digest
Verdict value as received and verification instant
outputs: Freshness assessment against the declared maximum age
preconditions: Evidence reference resolves to an external issuer
Subject digest matches the bound release digest or a mismatch is recorded
effects: Evidence index grows for the deployment
Stale or mismatched evidence is flagged, not overridden

functions.name: Compute delivery metrics
functions.description: Compute delivery metrics over this model's deployment records for a stated window and population, qualified by record coverage.
inputs: Window start and end with explicit offsets
outputs: Metric values with units and population sizes
preconditions: Required instants and outcome flags are present or explicitly counted as missing
Metric definitions are versioned
effects: A serial delivery metrics report is issued
Results below the coverage threshold are suppressed or caveated

functions.name: Project deployment to an external vocabulary
functions.description: Produce a projection of a deployment record into an external deployment vocabulary using the maintained mapping set, marking lossy and unmapped elements.
outputs: Non-conformance statement where terms are unstable
preconditions: A mapping entry exists for the requested vocabulary version
Stability levels of external terms are recorded
effects: A projection is emitted without altering the source record
Unmapped elements are reported rather than silently dropped

functions.name: Apply retention disposition marker
functions.description: Evaluate a deployment record against the adopting Dimension's retention policy and, where eligible, reduce it to a tombstone and emit a disposition marker for the storage owner to execute.
outputs: Disposition marker for the storage owner
preconditions: Retention clock start instant is recorded
No legal hold is active
The deployment is not current for any target
effects: Purged fields are removed and the tombstone retained
Execution of physical deletion is delegated to the adopting Dimension's storage policy

composition.purpose: A deployment installs a release. This model carries the pinned release reference, artifact coordinate and binding digest only; release identity, versioning, artifact content, SBOM, build provenance and release lifecycle remain owned by the target model.

A deployment targets a runtime environment. This model carries the pinned environment reference, the deployment-specific target selector and reported placement; environment definition, topology, capacity and environment lifecycle remain owned by the target model.
This model is a child of the parent software product or service model, which owns product identity, ownership and commercial context; this model adds only the installed-into-environment occurrence.

composition.target: Pipeline or automation run model (not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Carry an opaque reference to the run that requested the deployment so that change lead time can be anchored upstream; pipeline definition, orchestration and run lifecycle are not modelled here. No sibling model is registered, so this link is a declared structural gap.

composition.target: Change authorisation or configuration change control record (adopting-Dimension owned)
composition.purpose: Carry the authorisation reference and its received verdict at the deployment boundary; change workflow, impact analysis and approval lifecycle remain with the configuration change control regime.

Carry gate verdict references with issuer, policy identifier and verification instant; evaluation, policy authorship and enforcement are owned by the verifier and are explicitly not acquired by referencing them.

Align deployment kinds and the service and environment subject bindings to the CDEvents predicates and required subject fields, recorded as an alignment with mapping evidence, not as a conformance claim.

composition.target: OpenTelemetry deployment and service resource attributes
composition.purpose: Align environment tier naming and deployed-instance correlation to the stable deployment environment attribute and service instance identity, while flagging that deployment identifier, name and status attributes are not yet stable.
Align this model's runtime-phase assertions with the runtime lifecycle scope used for SPDX relationships, noting that SPDX defines a relationship scope rather than a deployment entity.

composition.target: ISO/IEC 19770-2 software identification tags via NISTIR 8060
composition.purpose: Align deployed-instance correlation with endpoint installed-software evidence so that observed installations can be reconciled to deployment records; tag production and asset inventory remain external.

composition.target: Fleet, device and over-the-air update deployment specialisation
composition.purpose: Permit a specialisation that adds device-cohort staging, update slot and offline-target semantics for embedded and device fleets, specialising only the deployment subject; generic identity, authority, lifecycle and conflict handling stay in this model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single system of record for deployment identifiers per environment class and register it as the authoritative master system.
The adopting Dimension must publish its retention period, hold authority and disposition executor for deployment records before the model is used in production.
The adopting Dimension must declare its state vocabulary version, its mapping from orchestrator-reported statuses, and the role permitted to extend that vocabulary.
The adopting Dimension must declare which environment classes are treated as production for access, sensitivity and metric purposes.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Deployment records are namespaced under the adopting Dimension's software domain path for this model (NAV.INF.SFT.DEP). Local element identifiers use lower-kebab-case with no date-like component; external identifiers are stored in their own scheme with an explicit scheme name and are never rewritten into the local namespace.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-sft-009 in the world-model record plane, model WM-SFT-009
Relation ledger planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv, covering the REFERENCE links to WM-SFT-008 and WM-SFT-010
Parent registry entry WM-SFT-002 for product and service context

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form orders keys deterministically, distinguishes an absent element from an empty one, and omits derived fields such as current-deployment flags from digest computation.

Identifiers are canonicalised to the highest available priority form and always carried with their issuing system reference; external coordinates and digests are normalised per scheme with the algorithm name retained.
Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and the original offset preserved; a derived normalised UTC value may be added alongside but never replaces the original offset.
patch_rules: State history is append-only: a patch may add a transition entry but may never rewrite or delete an existing one.

Once a deployment reaches a terminal state, its identity, binding references, binding digests and terminal instants are immutable; corrections are expressed as superseding entries carrying actor, reason and source reference.
Every patch records the asserting system, the reason and the ingestion instant; patches lacking provenance are rejected rather than applied with defaults.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional data elements, alignment entries or new non-terminal states is a minor change; consumers must ignore unknown optional elements.

Changing the state vocabulary semantics, the identity priority order, the current-deployment resolution rule or a field's cardinality from optional to required is a breaking change requiring a new major version.
Deprecated elements are retained for at least one major version with a documented mapping to their replacement before removal.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the deployment identifier assigned by the registered system of record for deployments in the adopting Dimension, stored together with a reference to that issuing system.
Governed global identifier or IRI: a resolvable identifier minted under a governed namespace when no master-system identifier exists.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, recorded as locally minted with its minting authority, used only when neither higher-priority identifier is available.
A date, a version string, a release tag, an environment name, a commit hash or an artifact digest is never used as the identifier of a deployment; digests are binding evidence, not identity.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 date-time with explicit seconds and an explicit numeric UTC offset or Z; date-only values, local wall-clock strings and values without an offset are rejected. Event time (requested, started, completed, superseded, failure onset, recovery completion) is recorded separately from observation time (when the reporting system saw the fact) and ingestion time (when this model received it); when only ingestion time is known, event time is left null rather than back-filled, and the original offset is preserved even where a normalised UTC value is also stored.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely history ledger entries and periodic delivery metrics reports, are named as artifact kind, then subject reference, then a zero-padded monotonic sequence unique per subject. Ordering derives from the sequence, not from any timestamp, and the covering interval is carried as explicit start and end fields rather than encoded into the name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest with a named algorithm over its canonical serialisation, plus the binding digest of the release it asserts. An artifact whose recomputed digest differs from the recorded digest, or whose binding digest disagrees with the referenced release, is quarantined as unverified and excluded from current-deployment resolution and from metric populations until re-verified by the record custodian.

policies: Reference, do not restate: facts owned by WM-SFT-008 and WM-SFT-010 are carried only as pinned references, binding keys and subject-specific parameters; local copies of target-owned attributes are prohibited.

Describe, do not orchestrate: the model records declared intent, received state and reported outcome; it never defines rollout mechanics, evaluates gates, enforces policy, or acts as an organizational audit trail.
Alignment, not conformance: external standards are recorded as versioned alignments with mapping evidence and stability levels; a conformance claim requires cited conformance evidence.
History is append-only and provenance-bearing: every recorded fact names its asserting system and capture path, and corrections supersede rather than mutate.

read: Reads resolve a deployment by its identifier or by target plus evaluation instant, returning the record with sensitivity-based redaction applied to parameter bindings and production target detail.
Reads of referenced release and environment content are resolved by dereferencing the target models; this model returns references and never a cached copy of target-owned attributes.
Every returned record states its confidence level, its ingestion instant, and whether any element is inferred rather than asserted.
create: A deployment record is created only with a resolvable release reference, a resolvable environment reference, a deployment kind from the controlled vocabulary and an identifier satisfying the identity priority order.
Creation appends an initial state transition entry and registers the record in the target's history ledger with a monotonic revision sequence.
Duplicate submissions matching the natural key tuple are merged or rejected under the declared deduplication rule rather than creating a second record.
update: Updates append state transitions, progress observations, evidence references and drift status; they never rewrite prior entries.
Terminal-state records accept only superseding correction entries carrying actor, reason and source reference.
Binding references and binding digests are immutable after the first transition out of the initial state.
delete: Deployment records are never hard-deleted while the record is current for any environment target; closure is by terminal state transition, not deletion.

After the adopting Dimension's retention period elapses and no legal hold is active, the record is reduced to a tombstone retaining the deployment identifier, issuing system reference, release and environment reference identifiers, terminal state and terminal instants; parameter values, actor identifiers, target host detail and free-text notes are purged.

This model declares disposition eligibility and emits a disposition marker; physical destruction of stored records is executed by the adopting Dimension's records-management and storage policy, which owns the deletion act.

Deletion of a referenced release or runtime environment is owned by WM-SFT-008 and WM-SFT-010 respectively and must never cascade into deployment records; the surviving deployment record marks the reference as dangling.
A legal hold or open investigation suspends disposition eligibility; only the retention and disposition role may set or release the hold.

responsibilities: Own the scope statement, boundary notes and state vocabulary
Approve breaking changes and version transitions

roles.name: Deployment record custodian

Apply deduplication, quarantine unverified artifacts and write correction entries
